title: FCH chemoton replicates on seed 3 (K layer rim/core 2.51, fed 2198 vs starved 357 amphiphile), but K-free rings also persist when fed; E holds by construction
summary: Fresh seed 3 (192^2, t=600): micelles condense from the noisy bath by t=24, open into bilayers and by t~200 settle into one double-walled vesicle with the catalyst beaded on its bilayer and two catalyst-free rings (rerun/sheet.png). labkit: K rim/core 2.51, rim/outside 6.49, membrane-like in aggregate; track #14 has K membrane-like at mid-life. Starvation fork on the same seed (world_starve.py, feed cut at t=300): total amphiphile 2542 at t=300 falls to 357 by t=600 against 2198 for the fed run; K 219 vs 1921 (totals_s3.txt); the K vesicle shrinks to a small ring. In the fed run the two K-free rings also persist to t=600, living on amphiphile from the bath.

observations.S: rerun/sheet.png t=0: noisy bath over the whole domain
observations.I: rerun/sheet.png t=207-600: three discrete vesicles that keep their identity
observations.B: rerun/FACTS.md: catalyst K rim/core 2.51, rim/outside 6.49, membrane-like; sheet shows K beads along the bilayer of the double vesicle

seeds_run.result: pass for S, I, B; fork replicates

controls_run.E: starve/ (feed cut at t=300, seed 3) vs rerun/: amphiphile 357 vs 2198 at t=600 (totals_s3.txt, totals_s3.png)

verdicts.limitation: E holds by construction (amphiphile is made only by K from the fed precursor and decays everywhere), as the claim itself says; the fork confirms the dependence but not an emergent metabolism. Only 3 individuals on this seed, and two of them carry no catalyst yet persist as long as the K vesicle, so persistence is not specific to the K-bearing vesicle here. I did not re-run the no-catalyst or no-gate arms.
